title: Bedrock Robotics nears $1B in total funding as demand for autonomous heavy equipment surges
summary: Bedrock Robotics has secured $600 million to scale autonomous heavy equipment and combat construction labor shortages.
points: San Francisco-based Bedrock Robotics has raised $600 million in Series C funding, co-led by CapitalG and Emergence Capital, at a $4.1 billion valuation.
The round brings its total funding to nearly $1 billion as it scales fully autonomous heavy equipment to address nationwide construction labor shortages.

The round included new investors US Innovative Technology Fund (USIT), Bessemer Venture Partners, and Temasek, alongside existing investors 8VC, Georgian, Valor Equity Partners, Xora, Eclipse, Perry Creek Capital, NVIDIA, and others.

title: OMRON to acquire OnLogic to address edge AI applications
summary: OMRON will add industrial computing from OnLogic to its industrial automation expertise to serve data- and AI-intensive applications.
points: OMRON Corp. this month said it has agreed to acquire 100% of OnLogic this week, worth $675 million, to combine its proven automation with OnLogic’s industrial computing expertise.
“This acquisition is an important step in advancing our SF2030 vision and our evolution toward GEMBA DX,” stated Junta Tsujinaga, president and CEO of OMRON.
“North America is a key growth market for OMRON, and this investment strengthens our foundation there while building the capabilities our customers will increasingly need.”

title: ETH Zürich Teaches a Humanoid to Climb, Vault and Recover by Planning Body Contacts
summary: Tested on a Unitree G1, the research combines human motion data and reinforcement learning to connect mobility skills using onboard terrain sensing.
points: With Rich Robinson, Clinical Professor of Entrepreneurship at Peking University

Researchers at ETH Zürich's Robotic Systems Lab and collaborators have demonstrated a Unitree G1 climbing ladders, scaling obstacles and recovering from falls with a single learned locomotion policy .

Their approach, Attention-based Contact Planning (ACP) , focuses on where the robot should place its body against the environment, allowing a controller to work out the movements between those contacts.
